visual_action: Hold on an immovable staircase; no mechanical motion.
vo: The one thing a staircase is guaranteed to do is stay where it is.

visual_action: The staircase begins moving and resolves into an escalator.
vo: An escalator is not a staircase.

visual_action: Crowded Hong Kong escalator climbs normally; passenger flow is legible.
vo: Watch this one in Hong Kong. About a hundred and twenty people are going up.

visual_action: Freeze the step band while passenger momentum continues a fraction.
vo: Then the steps stop.

visual_action: Reverse the band and visibly accelerate the crowd downhill.
vo: Then they come back down. Faster.

visual_action: Freeze the consequence and isolate the verified injury count.
vo: Eighteen people are injured before the machine finally stops.

visual_action: Open an official-case diagram with two linked failure positions.
vo: The investigation found two failures.

visual_action: The main drive chain fractures under load.
vo: First, a drive chain snapped.

visual_action: The detector remains inert while the broken chain warning reaches it.
vo: Then the device built to detect exactly that... failed as well.

visual_action: Push toward a small nut inside the detector but withhold the full mechanism.
vo: Buried inside the second failure was one ordinary nut.

visual_action: Hold the nut as an unresolved labelled object, then file it away.
vo: We will get to the nut in a bit.

visual_action: Lay out four failure cards with their protective devices concealed beneath.
vo: First: four ways an escalator can go horribly wrong — and the small army of machines that's supposed to stop them.

visual_action: Camera drops through the visible tread into the mechanism.
vo: Starting with what you are actually standing on.

visual_action: Mall cladding peels away to a clean systems cutaway.
vo: Strip away the construction and look.

visual_action: Strike out the familiar staircase silhouette.
vo: Not stairs.

visual_action: Reveal the complete returning step loop and both sprockets.
vo: More like a continuous chain carrying metal steps around sprockets at either end.

visual_action: Isolate one step, its two wheel sets and the two guide tracks.
vo: Each step rides on wheels following two tracks.

visual_action: Animate one step through flat, stair and flat states while the tread stays level.
vo: As those tracks change position, the tread stays level, rises into a staircase, then flattens at the landing.

visual_action: Follow the same step around the sprocket and along the underside return.
vo: After that, the step carries on beneath the floor. Upside down.

subbeat_action: Pull back to reveal the complete loop; begin returning the staircase facade.
visual_action: Pull back to the full loop carrying a crowd as the staircase facade returns.
vo: A conveyor belt powerful enough to carry a crowd of people uphill. It simply happens to be shaped like stairs.

visual_action: Zoom into the landing interface and mark moving versus fixed surfaces.
vo: Failure one is where the moving step meets the stationary floor.

visual_action: Highlight the step ridges beneath one ordinary shoe.
vo: Those ridges beneath your shoes have an important job at the landing.

subbeat_action: Introduce lace, coin and clothing silhouettes toward the comb.
visual_action: Macro mesh: comb teeth enter the grooves as three loose-object silhouettes approach.
vo: Their grooves mesh with the teeth of the yellow comb plate, leaving very little open space for a lace, coin or piece of clothing to follow the step underneath.

visual_action: Lift a lace and coin onto the stationary landing.
vo: Small objects are meant to be lifted clear instead.

visual_action: A trapped object pushes the comb plate backward.
vo: But if something jams, the comb plate can move.

visual_action: Measure the tiny travel, close the switch, then halt the entire loop.
vo: Barely. A few millimetres of movement operates a safety switch and stops the drive.

visual_action: Reduce the landing to a simple plate-switch diagram.
vo: The floor is the switch.

visual_action: Travel from the landing to the skirt gap beside the step.
vo: Failure two lives along the sides.

subbeat_action: Begin deforming soft objects toward the skirt gap.
visual_action: Magnify the millimetre gap, then deform soft objects toward it.
vo: Between each moving step and the fixed skirt panel is a narrow clearance. Only millimetres — but rubber, loose fabric and small fingers do not remain conveniently rigid.

visual_action: Reveal the brush in context beside an approaching shoe.
vo: So there are brushes. That stiff strip at ankle height.

visual_action: Strike out a shoe-cleaning interpretation.
vo: It is not cleaning your shoes.

visual_action: Brush contacts the shoe before it can reach the skirt gap.
vo: It is touching them BEFORE the machinery does.

visual_action: The shoe shifts away from the edge toward the safe centre.
vo: The brush warns you and nudges your foot toward the centre.

visual_action: An obstruction trips the secondary skirt safety path and stops the loop.
vo: On machines fitted with skirt-obstruction devices, something entering the gap can interrupt the safety circuit too.

visual_action: Resolve brush and switch as two sequential layers.
vo: The brush is the warning. The switch is the apology.

visual_action: Return to the step surface and mark the tread as the hazard.
vo: Failure three is the floor itself.

visual_action: Break one wheel or axle and let the step sag below its neighbours.
vo: A damaged wheel or axle can let a step ride too low.

visual_action: Hold on the sag, then move the danger marker forward.
vo: The dangerous part is not merely the sag beneath your feet.

subbeat_action: Split from the comb-strike outcome to the open-floor-gap outcome.
visual_action: Track the low step toward the comb and preview collision versus open-gap outcomes.
vo: It is that the damaged step is still travelling toward the comb, where it can strike the landing — or leave an opening where the floor should be.

visual_action: A fixed detector catches the lowered step before the landing.
vo: Step-sag devices are positioned to detect that drop and stop the machine.

visual_action: Follow an empty slot until a missing-step sensor stops it below the floor.
vo: Other systems can detect a missing step before the empty space returns to the passenger side.

visual_action: Collapse the three local hazards around one pair of shoes.
vo: Those first three failures begin at one pair of shoes.

visual_action: Pull from one pair of shoes to the entire loaded step band.
vo: Failure four involves everybody on the same moving staircase.

subbeat_action: Bring in drive restraint against the established gravity load.
visual_action: Show gravity pulling the passenger load downhill while the drive restrains it.
vo: A loaded descending escalator is not simply being carried by its motor. Gravity is helping too, and the drive is controlling the descent.

visual_action: Apply the normal brake at the motor and stop the connected system.
vo: The normal brake holds the machine when it stops.

visual_action: Sever the drive chain between motor and step band.
vo: But break the connection between the drive and the steps...

visual_action: Hold the motor still while the detached loaded steps begin moving downhill.
vo: and that brake may be holding the motor while the passengers are standing on something no longer attached to it.

subbeat_action: Add the broken-drive-chain detector on a separate path.
visual_action: Add the auxiliary brake and broken-chain detector on separate paths.
vo: That is why long or heavily loaded machines can carry a second brake farther down the drive system — plus a device specifically watching the main drive chain.

visual_action: Light the independent trigger inputs one at a time.
vo: Different triggers.

visual_action: Separate the protective devices spatially.
vo: Different mechanisms.

visual_action: Stack their protected ranges over the same passenger load.
vo: Overlapping protection.

visual_action: Strike through a decorative redundancy diagram.
vo: That is not belt and braces.

visual_action: Lock the independent safety architecture into one clean system view.
vo: That is the design.

visual_action: Return abruptly to the documentary case card.
vo: So. Hong Kong.

visual_action: Reconstruct the loaded escalator moving upward.
vo: The escalator was carrying about a hundred and twenty people upwards.

visual_action: Keep the load indicator inside its normal range.
vo: It was not overloaded.

visual_action: Show fatigue initiating and the main chain separating.
vo: Its main drive chain broke from metal fatigue, disconnecting the steps from their upward drive.

visual_action: Reverse the detached step band under the crowd's weight.
vo: The passengers' weight pulled the step band backwards.

visual_action: Trace the expected detector-to-auxiliary-brake path.
vo: The broken-chain device should have detected the failure and activated the back-up brake.

visual_action: Break the expected path before the brake.
vo: It did not.

visual_action: Macro cutaway: grease and dust bind the detector's sliding parts.
vo: Investigators found sticky grease — formed from lubricant and dust — obstructing its moving parts.

visual_action: Reveal both springs; the nut clamps one spring in place.
vo: One of its two compression springs had also been locked by a nut,

visual_action: The detector force gauge drops from two springs to one.
vo: cutting the force available to move the detector by roughly half.

visual_action: Isolate the ordinary nut at full scale.
vo: There is the nut.

visual_action: Replay the primary chain fracture as failure one.
vo: The chain broke.

visual_action: Complete the causal chain: fracture, jammed detector, absent auxiliary brake, reversal.
vo: But the accident happened because the machine assigned to notice the break... could not move.

visual_action: Return to an ordinary Everyman entering a calm escalator.
vo: Tomorrow, you will step onto an escalator without looking down.

visual_action: Pass the camera across the comb teeth as they perform normally.
vo: Past comb teeth meant to lift loose objects clear.

visual_action: Pass the brush as a shoe shifts toward centre.
vo: Past brushes telling your feet to move.

visual_action: Reveal the step-sag detector beneath the moving tread.
vo: Over detectors waiting for a step to sag.

visual_action: Continue through the machine room to the detector and auxiliary brake.
vo: Above a chain device and an auxiliary brake waiting for the drive to let go.

visual_action: Reassemble the cladding while the hidden devices remain faintly visible beneath.
vo: It feels like a staircase because all of them are working to keep it feeling like one.

visual_action: The protective overlays disappear; only the ordinary escalator remains.
vo: You will not notice any of them.

visual_action: Hold on the quietly moving escalator and end without a sign-off.
vo: and that is them working as designed.
